rationale: No candidate plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template for the brief White House concert invitation. C06 has the closest phrase-level resemblance in “I would like to extend,” but uses it in a lengthy commendation letter and shares neither the invitation formula nor the child’s operative structure. C20 and C03 contain similarly courteous presidential language, but their purposes and structures are materially different. Any overlap is generic correspondence boilerplate.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Mrs. Kennedy and I would like to extend an invitation to you
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I would like to extend my hearty thanks to you
shared_material.explanation: C06 shares the generic construction “I would like to extend,” but the object and communicative function differ, making this too routine to establish a drafting-template relationship.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I do hope you will honor us with your presence.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope to be with you at the ribbon cutting.
shared_material.explanation: C20 shares a generic closing expression of hope involving attendance, but reverses who is expected to attend and lacks the child’s invitation structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: your performance as one of the world's greatest artists would lend distinction
shared_material.explanation: C03 likewise praises the recipient or occasion before a courteous closing, but the language and administrative purpose are not distinctively parallel.
